evidence: The original diff has `const STALE_LOCK_MS: i128 = 10_000` inside claim_spawn_cooldown and `Duration::from_secs(10)` in try_acquire_spawn_lock, which is two encodings of one staleness policy. c7dc942 hoists one module-level `STALE_LOCK_MS: u64` that both use.
guidance_note: When a new function reuses a policy value that already exists in a neighbouring function, grep for the literal and hoist it before committing instead of declaring a second local constant.

evidence: False-positive flag: c7dc942 only touched Rust's STALE_LOCK_MS, and the cooldown branch in spawnAndWaitForReady came with the original PR. All four original cooldown tests target obtainDaemonKick, so the new obtainDaemon branch really was untested.
guidance_note: When a behavior gate is added at two call sites (kick path and async path), write at least one test per call site in the original PR.

evidence: c7dc942 hoisted STALE_LOCK_MS but added a comment saying it is 'Not check-protocol'd because it does not cross the wire'. The agent then conceded that 'doesn't cross the wire' was never the criterion, because SPAWN_COOLDOWN_MS and the filename are checked for the same shared-file reason. The F1 fix single-sourced the value inside Rust and left the cross-runtime mirror unchecked.
guidance_note: When single-sourcing a constant that the other runtime also defines, apply the same test the existing check-protocol rows use (does it govern a shared artifact?) before writing an exclusion rationale.

evidence: False-positive flag: 915189b changed only TS tests, and the Rust cooldown functions came with the original PR with no Rust tests. The agent extracted a pure cooldown_decision and pinned its boundaries instead of the reviewer's four fs-level scenarios. That covers the risky arithmetic more precisely.
guidance_note: When logic is mirrored across two runtimes, port the test scenarios to both in the original PR, not only to the one with the easier test harness.

evidence: False-positive flag: 915189b was tests only, and the `spawn on cooldown; daemon did not bind in time${reasonSuffix}` string came with the original PR. Appending '(lock-fallback)' to a failure whose cause is the cooldown gate does mislabel it. 7adca34 drops the suffix on that branch.
guidance_note: When adding an early-return branch to a function that takes a provenance suffix, decide explicitly whether the new failure reason inherits it.

evidence: The F2 fix (915189b) tested the cooldown branch only through the lock-held path. The agent rightly notes the gate is one seam, so per-path retesting is mostly structure. The real contract it pinned instead is the reasonSuffix handling unique to the lock-fallback path, so the premise is only partly right.
guidance_note: When adding tests for a new branch reached from several callers, enumerate the callers and the inputs that differ between them (here reasonSuffix) and cover each distinct observable in the same fix.

evidence: The F2 fix covered only the 'cooldown active' outcome on the async path. The garbage future-mtime outcome (spawn allowed, result 'started') was left untested there even though it was already tested on the kick path. claimSpawnCooldown is shared, so the gap is small but the observable differs.
guidance_note: When porting a test suite from one entry point to another, port every outcome of the shared decision (deny, allow, garbage-allow), not just the one the reviewer named.

evidence: False-positive flag: recordSpawnAttempt came with the original PR, and 7adca34 only changed the cooldown reason string and added tests. The reviewer itself says 'this isn't a runtime bug today' because both callers run after ensureStateDir. So this is a hidden-coupling and mirror-asymmetry concern, and making the primitive mkdir its parent like Rust's create_dir_all is a cheap, apt fix.
guidance_note: When writing a mirror of an existing primitive, copy its preconditions too (Rust's create_dir_all) so the two implementations ask the same things of their callers.

evidence: The 'attaches to the in-flight daemon' test added by the F2 fix (915189b) starts the fake daemon at 40ms. It could pass through the top-level attach path with the same observable result (attached, spawned=0). A 40ms race against a sub-ms gap is unlikely, so the premise is partly right. The agent widened the delay to 150ms rather than asserting the gate was hit, which is still timing-based despite the reply's claim of 'deterministically'.
guidance_note: When a test's observable is identical across two code paths, make the test assert which path ran (spy or distinguishing output) rather than relying on timing.

evidence: The F4 fix (7adca34) extracted Rust's cooldown_decision and pinned exact thresholds, but left the TS mirror tested only at interior points. A `<` versus `<=` drift in TS would not be caught. The agent's reply says it is 'Mirroring last round's Rust extraction on the Node side', so it acknowledges the fix covered only one runtime.
guidance_note: When fixing a finding on one side of a two-runtime mirror, apply the same extraction and boundary tests to the other runtime in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F8 but overstates the impact. It claims a fresh install's first claimSpawnCooldown 'will silently fail', yet F8 notes both callers run after ensureStateDir, and the write failure is logged. The agent's closing reply repeats the false 'two-un-gated-spawns-at-startup gap' claim, though the shared fix was right.

narrative: This PR adds a spawn-rate cooldown mirrored across Rust and Node. Every round from 1 to 3 had at least one finding against original code, so no round was avoidable outright. Still, each round from 1 onward also carried fix-caused findings. Most came from fixes that addressed exactly the named instance: the Rust-only constant hoist (F3), lock-held-only tests (F6, F7), a timing-fragile new test (F9), and a Rust-only boundary extraction (F10). Round 4 was a clean confirmation pass.
guidance_observations: The PR's central property is TS/Rust mirroring, yet tests, constants, and preconditions were repeatedly fixed on one side only, and the reviewer had to ask for the other side each time.

Test-gap findings came in a staircase (kick path, then async lock-held, then lock-fallback, then future-mtime, then boundaries), which an upfront path-by-outcome test matrix would have collapsed into one commit.

evidence: The original readStartTime mapped non-zero exit with empty stdout to `gone`, skipping the kill(pid,0) fallback, and hidepid or permission-denied can produce exactly that output for a live pid. The agent removed the over-claimed `gone` state instead of parsing stderr text. Every ambiguous outcome now defers to kill, which is sound and simpler.
guidance_note: When designing a result type from an external tool's exit codes, list what each code can and cannot prove before adding a variant that claims certainty.

evidence: False-positive flag: the unpinned `ps -o lstart=` launch came with the original PR, and 255f91a changed only the outcome mapping. lstart is strftime-formatted with locale-dependent day and month names, so the module's 'opaque, compared by equality' claim needed a deterministic generator. c4c058a pins LC_ALL=C.
guidance_note: When an external tool's output is used as an opaque equality key across processes, pin every environment input that affects its formatting at the call site in the original PR.

evidence: The F2 fix (c4c058a) pinned LC_ALL but passed `...process.env` through, so a differing TZ still changes how localtime renders the same instant. The reviewer's DST example is wrong: localtime renders a fixed instant with that instant's offset, so crossing a DST boundary does not change the string. The TZ-env and tzdata cases are real, so the premise is partly right, and the agent echoed the DST claim uncritically.
guidance_note: When pinning environment so a formatter is deterministic, enumerate every env var the formatter reads (LC_*, TZ) in one pass rather than only the one the reviewer named.

evidence: The catch-all detail expression `ps ${res.reason} (exit ${res.exitCode})` was written in the F1 fix (255f91a). The reviewer admits the rate-limited case is unreachable because process-fingerprint is absent from RATE_LIMITS, and that the verdict is correct either way, so pushing back is right. The real ground is unreachable code with no behavioral effect, not dataflow-not-control-flow.

False-positive flag: the 'lease unreadable → displaced' test came with the original PR, and c4c058a touched only process-fingerprint. Every sibling test asserts a distinguishing reason substring, and this one asserted only kind. Adding `toContain("unreadable")` closes that gap.
guidance_note: When writing a table of sibling tests, give each case the same assertions as its siblings.

narrative: This PR adds a pid+start-time fingerprint for socket leases. The agent handled F1 well by deleting the over-claimed `gone` state instead of parsing stderr. Round 2 included one real fix-caused finding: the locale pin was incomplete because TZ was not pinned. It also included one cosmetic, unreachable-path finding against F1's rewritten detail string, which was rightly declined. Round 2 also had an independent finding against original code, so no round was avoidable outright.
guidance_observations: The environment-determinism fix was done one variable at a time (LC_ALL, then TZ), which cost a review round that one pass over the formatter's inputs would have saved.
The agent accepted the reviewer's incorrect DST rationale along with the correct TZ fix, so a wrong mechanism now sits in the PR record.
